passages.text: Zip the zombie woke up with a big smile. He put on his party hat and his pink socks. Today was the day of the village dance, and he did not want to be late!
The farmer saw a zombie in her tomato patch. She grabbed her pitchfork and yelled for help. But the zombie only wanted to give her a hug and a flower. Why does nobody ever ask first?
Every night the zombies make a long conga line. They wiggle past the barn and around the old well. The cows like to watch, and the sheep tap their feet to the beat.
Gus the zombie has a pet ghost named Puff. Puff is small and round and loves to float over the pumpkins. When Gus feels sad, Puff does a little loop in the air.
The villagers lit their torches and ran down the hill. Was it a dragon? No, it was just a zombie who had lost his left sock. He waved and asked if anyone had seen it.
A dog named Biscuit followed the zombie all the way home. The zombie gave him a pat and a brain shaped cookie. Now they go for a walk together every night!
Zombies love brains, but not the way you think. In this village, brains are tiny pink snacks that taste like strawberry. The zombie keeps a jar of them by his bed.
The moon came up over the village, round and bright. A zombie in a bow tie stepped out to dance. He spun, he hopped, and he fell into a hay pile with a happy laugh.
Farmer Fran grows the biggest pumpkins in town. One night a zombie sat on one and sang a song to it. Fran came out in her robe and said it was the nicest song she ever heard.
Why do the villagers always run after the zombie? He only wants to say hello. Maybe tomorrow he will bring them all a cake, and they will finally sit down for tea.
The zombie opened his closet and looked at his hats. There was a tall hat, a round hat and a hat with a duck on top. Which one would you pick for a moonlit walk?
Run, zombie, run! The villagers are coming with pitchforks and lanterns. Hop over the fence, slide past the sleepy goats and duck behind the big red barn until they go home.
At the end of a long night, the zombie sat on the porch. He was tired but very happy. He had danced, he had hugged a cow, and he had found three shiny brains.

It's 9 o'clock, and the zombie can't find his left shoe. He looks under the bed, in the bath and inside 3 big orange pumpkins. At last he finds it on his pet ghost's head! Puff says it's a hat now, and he won't give it back.
The zombie's conga line had 12 dancers last night. There were 7 zombies, 2 cows, a goat and 2 very confused chickens. Nobody knew who started it, but nobody wanted to stop until the sun came up at 6.

Farmer Fran counted her tomatoes and got 48. The next morning she counted again and got 47. She didn't know a zombie had borrowed 1 to use as a red nose for the dance. He's planning to give it back on Sunday.

Don't worry about the villagers. They're loud, and they wave their torches a lot, but they've never caught a zombie in 200 years. That's because zombies are great at hiding in haystacks, barrels and even the farmer's laundry basket.

The Crypt Closet has 8 hats on the top shelf and 5 pets on the bottom. The zombie can't decide between the cowboy hat and the frog. Maybe he'll save 20 more brains and get both! Then he'd be the best dressed zombie in town.

Biscuit the dog thinks zombies are the best. He's waited by the gate every night for 2 weeks, with a stick in his mouth. When the zombie shows up, Biscuit's tail wags so fast it's just a blur, and they play fetch until 11.

Here's a zombie fact. Zombies don't like loud music, but they love slow songs. On Friday, 6 zombies sang under the farmer's window, and her cat clapped along. She's asked them to come back next week and bring 2 more singers.

The zombie's grandma knits him a new sweater every year. This year it's green with 10 pink brains on the front and a pocket for snacks. He's going to wear it to the village dance on the 31st, and he can't wait.

There are 100 steps from the crypt to the village green. The zombie counts them out loud every night, one by one. Last night he got to 99 and couldn't remember what came next, so he just danced the rest of the way.

It wasn't the zombie's fault that the cake fell over. He'd only tried to add 1 more candle, and the table was very wobbly. Still, he said sorry 5 times, helped clean it up and baked a new cake that's twice as big.

The zombie's pet ghost can float 30 feet up in the air. From there, Puff can see the whole village and every pumpkin in it. When the villagers come with pitchforks, Puff gives 2 quick whistles, and the zombie's off!

Who's that dancing on the roof at 2 in the morning? It's the zombie, and he's wearing 3 party hats at once. The owls think he's silly, but they can't stop watching. One of them even tries to dance too.

The zombie's best day ever went like this. He woke up at 8, ate 4 brain muffins and found a lucky penny in his sock. Then he hugged a cow, and the cow didn't even run away. It just mooed and asked for 1 more hug.

Zip's to-do list for tonight: find the lost sock, dance with the cows, and visit Farmer Fran. He finished the first two in 10 minutes. The third one (the visit) did not go well; Fran saw him, grabbed a pitchfork and chased him around the barn 3 times. Still, 2 out of 3 is not bad!

A villager peeked out of her window and called, "There's a zombie on the green!" Everyone grabbed a torch and ran outside. The zombie - who was only out for a walk - waved, tipped his hat and politely asked for directions to the pumpkin patch. (It was the wrong way.)

Recipe for brain muffins: 2 cups of flour, 1 cup of pink sugar & a pinch of moon dust. Mix it all up; bake it until the whole crypt smells like a birthday party. The zombie says they're 100% delicious (and the dog agrees). Share them with friends - or with a very surprised farmer.

Things a zombie should never do: trip over a pumpkin, sneeze in the conga line, or wake up the farmer's goat. Tonight our zombie did all three - in that order! The goat was not amused; it chased him all the way back to the crypt. Tomorrow: no pumpkins, no sneezing and no goats.

The pet ghost, Puff, has one rule: no sad faces allowed. If the zombie frowns, Puff flies in loops until he laughs so much his hat falls off. It works every time (well, almost every time). Last Tuesday it took 47 loops & one very silly song about a dancing moose.

Dear villagers: I am a zombie, but I am a nice one. I like hugs, dancing, brain-shaped cookies and long walks under the moon. Please put down the pitchforks; let's have a picnic on the green instead! Love, your friend from the crypt (the one in the purple hat).

Farmer Fran built a scarecrow to keep the zombie out of her corn. The next morning, she found the scarecrow wearing a party hat - and dancing a slow waltz with the zombie! "Well," said Fran, "at least the crows are gone." Then she put on some music & joined in.

How to do the zombie shuffle: step left, step right, then wiggle your arms like wet noodles. Next, spin around (very slowly, or you will get dizzy) and clap 2 times. Do it again & again until the sun comes up - or until the farmer wakes up, whichever comes first.

The village has a new sign: "No zombies on the green after 9:00." The zombies read it, nodded politely and held a long meeting in the barn. Then they made their own sign: "No villagers at the dance unless they bring snacks." So far, 14 villagers have brought cake.

Score card for tonight's chase: villagers 0, zombie 5. The zombie hid in a haystack, a pumpkin cart and (once) inside a very surprised scarecrow. Next week the villagers plan to bring more lanterns; the zombie plans to bring more jokes. (The jokes are mostly about cows.)

Puff the ghost wrote a little poem for the zombie: "Roses are red; brains are pink. You dance like a star - or so I think." The zombie read it 12 times in a row. Then he pinned it to his closet door, right next to his favorite hat.

At midnight the moon rose over the rooftops & the owls began to hoot softly. One by one, the zombies crept out (very, very quietly) for the big dance on the green. Nobody saw them - except the farmer's dog, who joined the conga line and danced until dawn.

What do zombies want? Not much: a warm hat, a good friend and maybe a brain-shaped cake with 3 candles. The villagers still do not believe it; they wave their torches every time a zombie walks by. Someday, maybe, they will stop, smile and say hello.
